tips.title: Selecting the Right Paint Type
tips.text: For scale models, acrylic paints from brands like Vallejo (Model Air, Model Color) and Tamiya offer the best balance between ease of use, adhesion, and finish. Acrylics dry quickly, clean up with water, and can be thinned with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for optimal flow. Enamels like AMMO by Mig Jimenez or Tamiya Enamels are suitable for touch-ups and fine details but require enamel thinner and dry slowly. Lacquers provide a gloss finish but can be challenging to work with due to their fast drying time.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Sandpaper Grits
tips.text: Start with 240-320 grit sandpaper for removing mold lines and scratches. Use 120 grit for filling gaps and 400+ grit for final smoothing before painting. For hard-to-reach areas, use sanding sticks or dental instruments. Always sand in the direction of the plastic's grain, and use water (for acrylics) or a suitable lubricant (for enamels) to prevent heat buildup.

tips.title: Filling Gaps: Vallejo Plastic Putty vs Tamiya Putty
tips.text: Vallejo Plastic Putty is a versatile, all-purpose putty that works well with Vallejo paints and cleans up easily with water. It's suitable for most plastic types and dries quickly. Tamiya Putty, however, is specifically designed for Tamiya polystyrene and bonds exceptionally well. It's harder to clean up but provides superior adhesion. For best results, use Tamiya Putty with Tamiya plastics and Vallejo Putty with other plastics.

tips.title: Photo-Etch vs Resin Detail Parts
tips.text: Photo-etch parts from brands like Eduard and ICM offer delicate, highly detailed parts that can enhance your model significantly. They require careful handling, bending, and attachment with super glue. Resin detail parts, often supplied by aftermarket companies like Arma Hobby and Clear Prop Models, provide exceptional detail but can be fragile and require careful preparation and handling. Choose photo-etch for thin, structural details like grab handles and ladders, and resin for complex, robust parts like engine detail sets.

tips.title: Decal Setting Solutions: Micro Set/Sol vs Mr. Mark Softer
tips.text: Micro Set/Sol is a classic decal setting solution that softens and adheres decals to curved surfaces. Apply Micro Sol with a soft brush, allow it to soak in, then gently rub off excess with a damp cloth. Mr. Mark Softer offers a faster, more aggressive approach, but it's less suitable for fine detail work. It's ideal for large, flat decals and hard-to-reach areas. For optimal results, use Micro Set/Sol for most decals and reserve Mr. Mark Softer for larger, flatter decals.
